summary.headline: Meenakshi India Q1 FY27 PAT rose to Rs 712 lakh (about 153% YoY), but about half of it came from other income; core garment EBITDA margin was about 3.4%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was Rs 3,224 lakh, down about 3.4% YoY and broadly stable. Reported PAT of Rs 712 lakh was driven mainly by other income of Rs 711 lakh, which management said is mark-to-market linked and may not recur. The garment (textile) segment operating profit improved to Rs 343 lakh from Rs 28.24 lakh a year earlier on a similar top line, with management citing better mix, pricing discipline and cost control. The company reports zero leverage, net worth of Rs 142.65 crore and about Rs 80 crore of cash and investments.

segments.name: Garment / Textile (premium bottomwear and outerwear)
segments.commentary: Operating profit Rs 343 lakh on revenue of Rs 3,224 lakh (about 10.6% operating margin including other items in the segment definition as presented). Cost of materials net of inventory change was about 45.7% of revenue vs about 48% last year; employee cost Rs 894 lakh, flat YoY; other expenses Rs 747 lakh, down 7.3% YoY.

guidance_outlook: FY27: target capacity utilisation of about 70% (vs 65% currently cited on pieces basis); management said Q1 margins are on track to return to pre-tariff levels.
FY27 margin direction: move back towards FY25 EBITDA margins; management said pre-tariff EBITDA margin will not be fully reached but targeted about 17% by FY28.

FY30 illustrative projection in presentation: revenue about Rs 500 crore and PAT about Rs 65 crore; management called these conservative, pending FTA operationalisation (EU FTA hoped operational in Q1 CY27; US situation unclear).
Capacity: plan to go from 18 lakh pieces to 38 lakh pieces; 80% utilisation is the trigger to add capacity.

Capex: about Rs 40-50 crore to FY30 in two phases of about Rs 20 crore each; first factory targeted around FY28 (may slip by a couple of months), second around FY30. Management called these ballpark figures.
capex_capacity: Current capacity cited at 18 lakh pieces, planned expansion to 38 lakh pieces; utilisation of 65% is on absolute pieces produced and can vary with product mix.
About two lines of spare capacity exist in current facilities; two more manufacturing units planned gradually, depending on demand.
First new factory: about Rs 20 crore, targeted FY28 (possible slippage of a couple of months); second factory: about Rs 20 crore, around FY30.
Sri Lanka contract manufacturing MOU in place (not yet used); Nepal flagged as future plan; next factory being considered outside India in Nepal, Vietnam or Sri Lanka.
demand_pricing: Revenue mix by geography: about 50-50 Europe and US historically; management said Europe is now closer to 60%, as US volumes slowed on tariffs and customer overstocking.
US customers retained after tariffs, but volumes reduced; discounts and shipment holds were used to protect customers, which compressed margins.
Customer concentration: top 5 clients about 70% of revenue; 12-20 active customers at any time.
Management positions the company in premium segment vs Bangladesh, Vietnam, Pakistan (mass market); competitors cited for premium are Turkey, Tunisia, Eastern Europe, Guatemala.
Domestic India business is minimal; management said it is less profitable and not planned.
LDP (landed duty paid) model being introduced as a small service with better margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why stay in premium bottomwear, and why were margins hit by tariffs despite premium positioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said premium bottomwear was chosen for quota-era history and competition from Turkey/Tunisia/Eastern Europe rather than mass-market countries; it claimed tariff burden sharing was lower than mass-market peers.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and timing for the incremental 20 lakh pieces?
qa_highlights.answer: Two factories of about Rs 20 crore each: first around FY28 (may slip a couple of months), second around FY30; total about Rs 40-50 crore, described as ballpark.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 utilisation and margin expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Target about 70% utilisation in FY27 and move towards FY25 EBITDA margins; about 17% margin targeted by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why the Sri Lanka contract manufacturing and overseas plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Sri Lanka MOU is a contingency for US tariff changes (country-of-origin flexibility), not yet used; Nepal, Vietnam and Sri Lanka being evaluated for the next plant. Management said Europe/UK demand is not being moved out of India.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY30 projection of Rs 500 crore revenue and Rs 65 crore PAT conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, conservative given FTAs not yet operational; includes Sri Lanka contract volumes but no quantified share was given.

qa_highlights.question: D2C plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Test marketing started, put on hold due to a patent issue with the SHORTSTOP brand; not much invested in the brand.

qa_highlights.question: Athleisure and women's wear plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Women's wear is an easy extension of men's bottomwear; athleisure needs supplier base development (mainly cotton with some man-made fibre), using similar machines; no separate plant planned.

qa_highlights.question: FY25 base and exceptional income?
qa_highlights.answer: FY25 revenue about Rs 155 crore (operational) and Rs 191 crore gross; EBITDA Rs 51 crore including Rs 12.5 crore exceptional gain from sale of agricultural land; PAT Rs 40 crore including exceptional item.
